title: Magnets Attract and Repel
seo_title: Year 3 Science: Magnets Worksheets (North and South Poles, Attract and Repel)
standard_text: Observe how magnets attract or repel each other and attract some materials and not others. Describe magnets as having two poles. Predict whether two magnets will attract or repel each other, depending on which poles are facing.
meta_desc: Free Year 3 science worksheets on magnets: north and south poles, attract and repel, predicting with bar magnets, magnet strength tests and uses of magnets. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Like poles repel; unlike poles attract.
key_sub: Magnetic force works at a distance.
body_html:
How to think about it

Magnets have a north pole and a south pole.

  • Like poles repel (N and N, S and S). Unlike poles attract (N and S).
  • Magnetic force acts at a distance, even through paper or water.
  • Test strength with paperclips; bigger magnets are not always stronger.
Example

N near N?

Like poles

Answer: repel

Example

S near N?

Unlike poles

Answer: attract

Common mistakes

  • Thinking a north pole attracts a north pole.
  • Thinking bigger magnets are always stronger.
  • Thinking magnets must touch to work.

faq.q: When do magnets attract or repel?
faq.a: Unlike poles (north and south) attract. Like poles (north and north, or south and south) repel.

faq.q: Do magnets have to touch to work?
faq.a: No. Magnetic force is a non-contact force. It acts across a gap and even through paper, card or water.

faq.q: How can you test which magnet is strongest?
faq.a: Count how many paperclips each magnet can hold in a chain, using the same paperclips each time. The one that holds the most is the strongest.
